findings.title: Stop rendering imported and edited post HTML without sanitization (stored XSS)
Stop calling `Kernel#open` on URLs (command injection / local file read)
Throttle remote fetches globally; unauthenticated requests can trigger unbounded fetches and feed polls
Handle feed items that have no `content`
Make `TopicEmbed.import` robust to concurrency, deleted posts and caller mutation
Fix the malformed `end if` in the ERB template
Use an exact origin check for `postMessage`
JS-escape the referer and send only its origin as the `postMessage` target
Don't rewrite protocol-relative URLs, and keep non-default ports correctly
Don't add `force: true` to migrations, and don't edit an already-shipped one
Disqus import regressed: lost category/created_at and now crashes on fetch errors
Controller spec mocks `TopicRetriever`, but the controller enqueues a job

response: ## 1) Severity: CRITICAL | Type: Security Title: Stop rendering imported and edited post HTML without sanitization (stored XSS) Affected: - app/models/post.rb:131-133 - app/models/topic_embed.rb:13,22,36 - app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35 - app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19 Explanation: For `raw_html` posts, `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged. Nothing on the import path sanitizes that HTML: - `PollFeed` passes RSS item content straight to `TopicEmbed.import`. - It first runs `CGI.unescapeHTML`. That turns entity-escaped text such as `<script>` into live markup. - `import` also interpolates `url` unescaped into an ``, so a quote in the URL breaks out of the attribute. The resulting HTML is shown verbatim in the forum and in the embed view (`raw post.cooked`). `cook_method` also stays `raw_html` on later revisions. Anyone who can edit such a post (the owner, staff, or wiki editors) can save arbitrary HTML and script through the normal editor. Whoever controls the feed or the remote page, or is allowed to edit these posts, gets XSS on the forum origin. Proposed fix: ~~~ruby # post.rb return sanitize_html(raw) if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html] # e.g. Sanitize with a strict whitelist # topic_embed.rb link = "#{ERB::Util.html_escape(url)}" # and do not CGI.unescapeHTML feed content; sanitize instead ~~~ ## 2) Severity: HIGH | Type: Security Title: Stop calling `Kernel#open` on URLs (command injection / local file read) Affected: - app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 - app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 - lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148 Explanation: `open(url)` uses `Kernel#open`: - A string starting with `|` runs a shell command. - A plain path reads a local file. `import_remote` is a public method that does not validate its input. The Disqus task calls it with `t[:link]` taken from an imported XML file, so a crafted export can execute commands. `topic_embed.rb` also never requires `open-uri`. It only works if `poll_feed.rb` happened to load first. Otherwise `open(url)` tries to read a local file and the import fails. Proposed fix: ~~~ruby require 'open-uri' uri = URI.parse(url) raise Discourse::InvalidParameters.new(:url) unless %w[http https].include?(uri.scheme) html = uri.open.read ~~~ ## 3) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Security Title: Throttle remote fetches globally; unauthenticated requests can trigger unbounded fetches and feed polls Affected: - app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15 - lib/topic_retriever.rb:21-45 Explanation: The only gate is the `Referer` header, which any client can spoof. Every request for an unknown `embed_url` does two things: - It enqueues a job. - That job synchronously runs the full `PollFeed` and then an HTTP fetch. The throttle is keyed per URL. An attacker who varies the path or query on the allowed host bypasses it entirely and causes unlimited outbound fetches, feed parses and topic creation. Any page on the allowed host becomes a topic. The loading page also reloads itself every 30 seconds, so each open tab enqueues another job. Proposed fix: - Add a global rate limit on retrievals, plus per-IP limits in the controller. - Do not run `PollFeed` inline for every miss. - Consider requiring that URLs come from the feed, or match an allowed path pattern. ## 4) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug Title: Handle feed items that have no `content` Affected: - app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31-37 Explanation: RSS 2.0 items usually provide `description`, not `content`. When `content` is missing, `i.content.scrub` raises `NoMethodError` on `nil`. Because of that, the whole poll aborts and later items are never imported. A missing or nil title will also produce invalid topics, since validations are skipped. Proposed fix: ~~~ruby body = i.content || i.description next if body.blank? || i.title.blank? content = body.scrub ~~~ ## 5) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug Title: Make `TopicEmbed.import` robust to concurrency, deleted posts and caller mutation Affected: - app/models/topic_embed.rb:13-41 Explanation: - **Caller mutation:** `contents << ...` mutates the caller's string, and raises on frozen strings. - **Race on create:** Two concurrent imports of the same URL (the job plus the poller) both see no embed. One of them then raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` on the unique index, after its topic has already been created. - **Deleted posts:** If the embedded post was deleted, `embed.post` is `nil` and `PostRevisor.new(nil)` crashes. - **SHA updated on failed revision:** `content_sha1` is updated even when `revise!` returns false. Proposed fix: ~~~ruby contents = contents.dup << "..." # rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique and reload the embed return nil if post.blank? embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1) if revisor.revise!(...) ~~~ ## 6) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug Title: Fix the malformed `end if` in the ERB template Affected: - app/views/embed/best.html.erb:2-6 Explanation: `<%- end if %>` is not just `end`. Ruby treats the next compiled statement as the condition of a trailing `if`, so the whole if/else block becomes conditional on the buffer append for the following markup. It only works by accident and is fragile. Proposed fix: ~~~erb <%- end %> ~~~ ## 7) Severity: LOW | Type: Security Title: Use an exact origin check for `postMessage` Affected: - app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 Explanation: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring test. For example, if `discourseUrl` is `https://forum.example.com/`, the attacker origin `https://forum.example.co` passes the check. Today the impact is limited to resizing the iframe, but the pattern is unsafe to build on. Proposed fix: ~~~js var a = document.createElement('a'); a.href = discourseUrl; var expected = a.protocol + '//' + a.host; if (e.origin !== expected) { return; } ~~~ ## 8) Severity: LOW | Type: Security Title: JS-escape the referer and send only its origin as the `postMessage` target Affected: - app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11 Explanation: `request.referer` is HTML-escaped but not JS-escaped inside a script string. Separately, the responses are publicly cached (`discourse_expires_in`), so a cached page can embed the referer of a different requester. That breaks the target origin, and a cached response can also bypass the per-request referer check. Proposed fix: ~~~erb '<%= j(URI(request.referer).tap{|u| u.path=''; u.query=nil}.to_s rescue '') %>' ~~~ Also make these responses private and not cacheable, or add `Vary: Referer`. ## 9) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug Title: Don't rewrite protocol-relative URLs, and keep non-default ports correctly Affected: - app/models/topic_embed.rb:57-73 Explanation: - `//cdn.example.com/x.png` starts with `/`, so it gets rewritten to `http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png`, which is a broken link. - The port is dropped whenever it is 80 or 443, regardless of scheme. For example, `http://host:443` loses its port. Proposed fix: ~~~ruby if href.start_with?('/') && !href.start_with?('//') prefix << ":#{uri.port}" unless uri.port == uri.default_port ~~~ ## 10) Severity: LOW | Type: Maintainability Title: Don't add `force: true` to migrations, and don't edit an already-shipped one Affected: - db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:3 - db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 Explanation: `force: true` silently drops an existing table and its data. Editing a migration that has already been released also diverges schema history between installs. Proposed fix: ~~~ruby create_table :topic_embeds do |t| ~~~ Revert the change to the `top_topics` migration. ## 11) Severity: LOW | Type: Implementation Title: Disqus import regressed: lost category/created_at and now crashes on fetch errors Affected: - lib/tasks/disqus.thor:113-148 Explanation: - The `--category` option and the original `created_at` were removed, so imported topics now get the current date and no category. - Each thread now makes a network fetch. A single 404 or timeout raises an exception and aborts the whole import. Proposed fix: - Pass `created_at` and `category` through `import_remote`. - Rescue fetch errors per thread and skip that thread. ## 12) Severity: LOW | Type: Test Title: Controller spec mocks `TopicRetriever`, but the controller enqueues a job Affected: - spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:40-46 Explanation: The controller calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`. The spec only passes if jobs run inline in the test environment, so it couples to that config rather than to the controller's behavior. Proposed fix: ~~~ruby Jobs.expects(:enqueue).with(:retrieve_topic, has_entry(embed_url: embed_url)) ~~~

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate: Rendering imported and edited post HTML without sanitization allows stored XSS - Post#cook returns raw unchanged for raw_html posts, PollFeed passes RSS content to TopicEmbed.import without sanitization, CGI.unescapeHTML converts entity-escaped text into live markup, and URL is interpolated unescaped into href attribute
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the XSS vulnerability due to unescaped URL interpolation in the generated HTML, which matches part of the golden comment. However, the golden comment also mentions a NoMethodError if contents is nil, which the candidate does not address. The candidate focuses primarily on the XSS/sanitization issues and mentions the URL interpolation problem specifically. Since the XSS vulnerability from unescaped URL interpolation is identified in both, this is a partial match on the security issue, but misses the nil handling bug.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate: Malformed end if in ERB template - <%- end if %> treats next compiled statement as condition of trailing if, only works by accident
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same issue: the ERB block uses 'end if' which is invalid/problematic Ruby/ERB syntax. The golden comment says it's 'invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render' while the candidate says it 'treats next compiled statement as condition of trailing if, only works by accident'. Both are pointing to the same malformed 'end if' syntax problem and both indicate it should just be 'end' to properly close the if block.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate: RSS 2.0 items with description but no content cause NoMethodError on nil when calling i.content.scrub, aborting the whole poll
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same problem as the golden comment: calling i.content.scrub when i.content is nil (because RSS feeds may only have description, not content) will cause an error (NoMethodError/nil pointer exception). Both issues point to the same bug - the code assumes content is always populated when it may not be.

false_positives.candidate: Kernel#open called on URLs allows command injection (strings starting with | run shell commands) and local file read (plain paths read local files) - import_remote is public and doesn't validate input
topic_embed.rb never requires open-uri so it only works if poll_feed.rb loaded first, otherwise open(url) tries to read a local file

Remote fetches lack global throttling - throttle is keyed per URL so varying path or query bypasses it, allowing unlimited outbound fetches, feed parses and topic creation from unauthenticated requests with spoofed Referer header
Loading page reloads every 30 seconds causing each open tab to enqueue another job
Missing or nil title produces invalid topics since validations are skipped
TopicEmbed.import mutates caller's string with contents << which raises on frozen strings
Race condition on create - two concurrent imports of same URL both see no embed, one raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique after topic already created
If embedded post was deleted, embed.post is nil and PostRevisor.new(nil) crashes
content_sha1 is updated even when revise! returns false

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
